title: Decentralized prompt-steward checkpoints and CI gating for golden datasets
creator: Sanjay Patel
description:
Problem: Model/config rollouts occasionally introduce regressions that are only detected after production traffic. Current golden dataset workflow is centralized, manual, and slow to sign off; rollouts lack fine-grained CI gates tied to steward-approved prompt snapshots.

Goal: Implement a decentralized stewarding model that lets domain owners create signed checkpoint snapshots of golden prompt sets and associated metadata. Integrate these checkpoints into the CI/CD pipeline so that any config/model change triggers a deterministic regression evaluation against the stewarded snapshot. Provide RBAC, immutable checkpoint artifacts, and an automated rollback/annotation flow if regressions exceed thresholds.

Out of scope: UI polishing for console display (follow-up ticket), enterprise SSO integration (handled by dedicated private deployment tickets).
acceptance_criteria: Domain-level prompt stewards can create and commit immutable 'checkpoint' artifacts that include prompt set version, metadata, and signer identity.
Checkpoint artifacts are signed (HMAC) and stored with content-addressable IDs in the golden dataset registry.
CI integration: model/config change pipeline automatically runs regression evals against the latest checkpoint for affected domain and produces pass/fail verdict based on configurable thresholds.
Failed CI gate prevents rollout and posts automated annotation with the top 3 failure categories and example prompt/responses.
Audit log entries for checkpoint creation, CI gating decisions, and rollback actions are available to Console trace and exported to the audit sink.
Basic RBAC: only users in 'prompt-steward' role for a domain can create checkpoints; readers can reference checkpoints but not alter them.
Performance: CI step completes within 20 minutes for standard smoke eval (1000 samples) or falls back to asynchronous gating with clear flagging in the rollout UI.
technical_design_notes: Checkpoint schema: {prompt_set_id, revision, steward_id, timestamp, hmac_signature, sample_manifest_uri, metrics_baseline_uri, ttl_policy}. Implement as flat JSON stored in S3 with SHA256 key. (We will store manifest URIs, not embed large blobs).

Signing: use platform KMS-backed HMAC keys per org; default to service key when org key absent. CLI will expose 'redwood checkpoint create --domain=payments --signer=maria' that uploads manifest and returns content-addressable id.
Registry: extend golden-dataset service with endpoint /checkpoints/{domain}/latest and versioned listing; ensure immutability by write-once semantics and object-lock on S3 bucket.

CI: add new pipeline step 'eval-checkpoint' that fetches checkpoint manifest, runs eval harness (dockerized), compares metrics delta using the same metric definitions as Optimize, returns structured verdict with top N counterexamples.

Rollback flow: CI failure posts to rollout service with 'blocked-by-checkpoint' tag; engineers can run 'redwood rollout abort --reason=checkpoint-regression' which triggers rollback policy and alerts owners.
RBAC: map prompt-steward role to existing IAM groups; enforce via registry API token-scoped endpoints. We will reuse early design from PM-20488 for ACL mapping.
Cost: default smoke eval sample size 500 to limit GPU minutes in CI; allow domain override for critical domains.
Observability: emit events to Console trace with checkpoint_id, commit_hash, model_variant, latency and accuracy deltas, and test-run artifacts url.
Data retention: checkpoint manifests kept indefinitely; sample evaluation artifacts TTL=90 days unless steward requests longer retention.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): implement registry endpoints and CLI checkpoint create flow; disable CI gating by default; feature-flag backend.
Phase 1 (canary): enable CI gating for two low-risk domains (search-relevance, chat-routing) with synthetic traffic; invite 3 stewards to create checkpoints and validate pipeline.
Phase 2 (opt-in): allow engineering teams to opt-in by adding 'checkpoint-domain' label to their rollout config; provide onboarding doc and small workshop.
Phase 3 (required): flip default gating on for all domains after 4 weeks of stable runs and PM sign-off; expose clear override with audit trail for emergency rollouts.
test_plan: Unit tests for checkpoint manifest validation and HMAC verification.
Integration tests for write-once registry semantics using localstack S3 runner in CI.
E2E smoke: simulate model change pipeline using historical model A->B pair and verify CI step detects delta and produces identical failure summary as offline eval.
RBAC: tests to ensure non-steward cannot create or delete checkpoints; steward can list and create.
Load: verify checkpoint listing endpoints return <200ms for 95% p95 under 1000 concurrent reads.
Manual review: PM & Design sign-off on failure annotation UI snippet and message copy before Phase 2.
